claim: Elasticity framework: output elasticity is decomposed into a probability channel and a capital channel, with a queueing multiplier only where near-capacity utilisation is evidenced.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: Y = N x PoS (steady state). Probability channel eps_P = 10 x ((1-PoS)/PoS) x f x theta, with PoS=0.12 [E-3002] so (1-PoS)/PoS = 7.33; f = share of attrition attributable to the factor; theta = pass-through of a 10% factor improvement into that attrition class. Capital channel eps_C = 10 x c x tau x delta, with c = share of capitalised cost the factor touches, tau = fraction of that cost responsive to the improvement, delta = marginal-program quality discount (0.4-0.8). Time-only gains are credited to output ONLY through eps_C (fixed-budget program count) because a shorter step raises the steady-state approval rate only if it frees capital or capacity; a purely parallelisable speed-up produces a one-off level shift, not a rate change.

derivation: eps_P = 10 x 7.33 x f x theta with f=0.45 (efficacy share of failures [E-3012]) and theta=0.15-0.45; = 4.9 to 14.8. Capital channel negligible. Point 9.9 rounded to 10. theta band reflects that a 10% reduction in the share of programs on non-translatable targets is not fully observable ex ante.

Add a queueing multiplier of 1.3-1.6 because 48% of sites under-enrol or enrol nobody [E-3020] and >80% of trials miss the enrollment timeline. Total 1.5-4.0, point 2.5.

Sign caution: reducing fragmentation itself (looser eligibility) would lower PoS via lost enrichment, so the elasticity is only positive when defined as screening efficiency.

Add up to 0.9 for evidence-standard effects (acceptance of NAM and biomarker evidence) which are more properly attributed to B2 and B15. claim: B6 manufacturing elasticity at whole-system level is 0.8-3.5% per 10% improvement, point 1.8%; for autologous cell therapy alone it is 15-40%, point 25%.

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: System level: cell and gene therapy is roughly 10-15% of clinical programs. Within that segment eps is high because utilisation evidence is unambiguous (only 60% of candidates secured a slot [E-3038]; 25% manufacturing failure in NHL [E-3034]) - a 10% throughput gain converts near one-for-one into treated patients and into avoided program deaths, giving 15-40%. Weighting 0.125 x 25 = 3.1, discounted by 0.4-0.6 because much of the CGT gain accrues to commercial supply rather than to approvals, giving 1.3-1.9; band widened to 0.8-3.5 for ADC conjugation and fill-finish tightness [E-3039]. derivation: This channel is close to linear: annual approvals Y = N x PoS and N is set by capital. A 10% increase in deployable capital (or equivalently 10% better capital efficiency) raises N by 10%, discounted by marginal-program quality delta=0.4-0.8, giving 4 to 8. claim: Amdahl ceiling: eliminating discovery entirely removes at most about 30-40% of total elapsed development time and leaves cumulative PoS unchanged unless target and toxicity selection also improve.

claim: Elasticity comparison: using the published decision-theoretic result that +0.1 absolute predictive validity beats a 10x throughput gain, a 10% wet-lab throughput improvement is worth about +0.0041 of predictive validity, whereas a 10% relative improvement in predictive validity from a base r of 0.3-0.6 is worth 0.03-0.06 - making assay validity roughly 7 to 15 times (central 12x) more elastic than throughput for the same proportional effort.
source_title: Derived elasticity comparison, throughput vs predictive validity

figures.metric: predictive-validity equivalent of a 10 percent throughput gain
figures.denominator_def: equivalence derived from the published statement that +0.1 correlation exceeds a 10x (i.e. +900%) throughput change

derivation: From [E-7061], delta_r = 0.1 is at least as valuable as a factor-10 throughput change. Treating the throughput benefit as approximately logarithmic (in the rare-positive regime the number of candidates that must be screened per true positive scales with log throughput), the validity-equivalent of a throughput factor f is delta_r_eq = 0.1 * ln(f)/ln(10). For f = 1.1 (a 10 percent throughput gain): 0.1 * 0.09531/2.30259 = 0.00414. A 10 percent relative improvement in predictive validity gives delta_r = 0.03 at r=0.3, 0.04 at r=0.4, 0.05 at r=0.5, 0.06 at r=0.6. Ratios: 0.03/0.00414 = 7.2; 0.04/0.00414 = 9.7; 0.05/0.00414 = 12.1; 0.06/0.00414 = 14.5. Hence validity is 7-15x (central ~12x) more elastic than throughput for equal proportional effort. If the throughput benefit saturates rather than remaining logarithmic, the multiple is larger; if it were linear in f the multiple would fall below 1, but a linear reading contradicts the source statement in [E-7061] that +0.1 correlation outperforms a full 10x throughput change. This is a derived elasticity from a published simulation, not a measured elasticity on approval counts.

Santos gives 667 human protein targets of approved drugs [E-9500], IDG gives fewer than 700 against about 4500 druggable-genome genes [E-9501]. The two agree to within 5 percent. derivation: Against the historical 37 percent benchmark the AI-minus-benchmark difference is +0.03; against the contemporaneous 28 percent Citeline figure it is +0.12, a fourfold difference in effect size arising purely from comparator selection.
